source.title: Learning Curves for SGD on Structured Features

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no material cut-off or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: It compares convolutional and fully connected networks and varies batch size using learning-curve measurements, which conceptually tests parts of V3 and V5. It does not test random-label memorization or the fixed-epoch comparison in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results bearing on architecture and batch size. It does not report random-label fitting, optimizer comparisons, explicit regularization, width sweeps, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Cited results from other papers are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares convolutional and fully connected networks trained with SGD on CIFAR-10, reporting test MSE learning curves relevant to V3. Its online fixed-sample-budget batch comparison does not test V5's fixed-epoch claim for classifiers trained on a fixed dataset.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate, with a scope qualification: the theory predicts average test-loss dynamics from feature geometry and accurately describes the studied random-feature models and wide networks in the lazy-training regime. The convolutional network has a better CIFAR-10 test-loss decay exponent than the MLP. Extending the account to feature-learning networks remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes SGD learning curves in feature models and wide networks, rather than testing random-label memorization or the interventions in most listed versions. Its batch-size comparison uses a fixed compute budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that feature structure, learning rate, and batch size affect learning curves; the preferred batch size depends on feature correlations and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed online sample/compute budget, intermediate batch sizes are preferable for MNIST random ReLU features; the optimum depends on learning rate and feature structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For online SGD on structured features, batch size trades update count against gradient noise at a fixed sample budget.

record.problems: The architecture comparison reports qualitative exponent differences but not exponent values in the text. The batch-size finding is described at fixed compute, not fixed epochs; exact batch sizes and losses are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results omitted. Figure 3(e) also describes batch size changing average test loss and variance, but does not state the direction of the effect; it is not separately extracted because the fixed-compute MNIST result in R2 is the clearer reported batch-size outcome.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels; chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.

Classification-error comparisons at convergence; attribution to local connectivity; sparse local connections learned by fully connected networks; initialization from trained convolutional networks; architecture comparisons on the other named datasets.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning or optimizer interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets on fixed training sets, and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: A faster loss-decay exponent does not by itself establish lower converged classification error. The fixed-compute batch result warrants no V5 verdict, including no limits_scope label.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
MNIST architecture comparison; sparse local connections and convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Large versus small batches under a fixed epoch budget; recipe adaptations including warmup and normalization or regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: CONV
rows.operation_detail: Compared convolutional-network test-loss scaling with a fully connected network on CIFAR-10.
rows.value: CNN obtains a better exponent due to its faster decaying task spectra.
rows.note: The paper describes the comparison and its explanation; it does not state the exponent values in the text.
rows.check: Figure 5(f) reports test MSE learning curves and a better decay exponent for CONV than MLP, rather than classification error or a converged endpoint. Appendix J specifies fixed-learning-rate SGD with one-hot targets and 6000 sampled training examples; Section 5 gives a different sample count for spectral estimation. Keep the architecture result restricted to the reported learning curves.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, Figure 5(d)-(f) and accompanying paragraph; Appendix J.

rows.subject: MNIST ReLU random feature model
rows.operation_detail: Varied minibatch size at a fixed compute budget and compared test loss.
rows.value: Intermediate batch sizes are preferable on real data.
rows.uncertainty: Dots average and standard deviation for 30 runs.
rows.note: The text reports the qualitative result for the real-data curve but does not state the batch-size values or test-loss values. The fixed-compute comparison does not establish the fixed-epoch result in V5.
rows.check: This is online learning with a fixed budget of sampled examples/gradient evaluations, C = tm = 100, rather than fixed epochs over a fixed training set. It measures binary MNIST 8-versus-9 test MSE in a random-feature model. Intermediate optimal batch sizes do not establish an incomplete V5 effect. Figure 1(f) also separates learning rates 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5, which the row omits.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 convolutional versus fully connected networks trained with fixed-learning-rate SGD in the studied lazy-training regime
relationships.reason: R1 reports lower convolutional test MSE in Figure 5(f) and a faster test-loss decay exponent; support concerns these learning curves.
relationships.display_finding: CNNs had lower test MSE and faster test-loss decay; classification-error endpoints and numerical decay exponents were not established.
